Chapter Four: Humor, Humility, and the Limits of Literalism.
Over the next few months, something unexpected happened—the experimenter realized just how important it was to have a sense of humor about the whole thing. Believe it or not, some instructions turned out to be so impractical—or just plain ridiculous—that sometimes, the only way to cope was to laugh.
Picture this: sitting on the roof during menstruation. On one hand, it’s a quirky nod to those ancient purity laws. On the other, it’s a hilarious reminder of how wildly different modern life is from the world of the Bible.
Neighbors would sneak glances, maybe a little amused, maybe a little confused. Family members? They mostly shook their heads, probably wondering what on earth was going on. But here’s the thing—in those awkward, slightly embarrassing moments, there was a surprising sense of freedom.
When you’re faced with the impossible, you start to loosen your grip on perfection. You learn, pretty quickly, to let go and just embrace the messiness of real life.
There was another big lesson, too: the value of humility. Trying to follow every single instruction made it clear just how easy it is to judge someone else for not measuring up. But honestly, not a single person can live out every command perfectly—not even the most devoted believer you know.
Even the Bible is full of people who stumble, who question, and who struggle to figure out what God actually wants.
Maybe the most powerful moment came with realizing that literalism only takes you so far. If you try to follow every rule, no matter how well-intentioned you are, you can end up in some pretty absurd—or even harmful—situations. Suddenly, it’s obvious that being faithful isn’t about rigid obedience. It’s about seeking wisdom, showing compassion, and working for justice.
And you know what? In conversations with friends and even total strangers, the experimenter noticed something universal. Most people are craving honesty. They want to hear that it’s okay to question, to doubt, or even to laugh at the parts that just don’t make sense. Admitting uncertainty didn’t feel like weakness anymore—it actually became a real source of strength.
By the end of this phase, the experimenter learned to hold the Bible—and herself—a little more lightly. The journey stopped being about proving a point, and turned into a chance to discover the beauty and complexity of faith.
The year wasn’t over yet, but already, something important was clear: searching for “biblical womanhood” isn’t really about finding perfect answers. It’s about learning to live gracefully with the questions.
